post.description: Synchronous: Cloud submits every runtime operation and waits (up to 45s, so use a client timeout of at least 60s) before responding. 502 harness_error lists per-item results in error.detail.operations[]; 504 beeos_harness_update_in_progress means work continues, retry the identical request after Retry-After (a create without an Idempotency-Key is not re-attached and would create a second harness); 409 beeos_harness_busy means a different write is in flight, retry after Retry-After; 409 beeos_idempotency_conflict means the Idempotency-Key was used with a different request; 503 harness_unavailable means the instance is not running or the operation journal is unavailable; 413 means the body exceeds 4 MiB (upload large skills as a Files blob). The optional Idempotency-Key header (1-128 visible ASCII characters) makes a create (POST, or PUT with template_id) safe to resend: the same key and request returns the same harness. instance_id and name are required and base must equal the instance runtime (422); template_id and template_version create the harness from an agent template; default_model is honored only here. a non-empty skills or mcp_servers is rejected on create (422 beeos_field_not_supported); add them with PUT. Not supported by BeeOS Cloud yet (422 beeos_field_not_supported): a non-empty system_prompt, disabled_tools, environment or plugins, or any max_step or timeout_seconds. An unchanged name and empty values are accepted, so a GET-modify-PUT round trip works.

put.description: Synchronous: Cloud submits every runtime operation and waits (up to 45s, so use a client timeout of at least 60s) before responding. 502 harness_error lists per-item results in error.detail.operations[]; 504 beeos_harness_update_in_progress means work continues, retry the identical request after Retry-After (a create without an Idempotency-Key is not re-attached and would create a second harness); 409 beeos_harness_busy means a different write is in flight, retry after Retry-After; 409 beeos_idempotency_conflict means the Idempotency-Key was used with a different request; 503 harness_unavailable means the instance is not running or the operation journal is unavailable; 413 means the body exceeds 4 MiB (upload large skills as a Files blob). The optional Idempotency-Key header (1-128 visible ASCII characters) makes a create (POST, or PUT with template_id) safe to resend: the same key and request returns the same harness. An absent field is unchanged; a present list replaces the whole list. When skills is present it is diffed against the installed skills: listed skills with files, content or blob (exactly one) are installed; an installed skill listed with a different enabled flag is updated; installed skills that are omitted are uninstalled unless bundled with the runtime; a listed skill that is not installed and has no files, content or blob returns 422; enabled:false on a fresh install returns 422. When mcp_servers is present it is diffed against the runtime MCP servers: a server sent with a credential (headers or auth plus expires_at, at most 24 hours ahead) is set, a connected server sent without one is kept, omitted servers are unset; the url must be https and transport is http or sse; GET never returns a url or credential. 422 beeos_mcp_not_supported is returned only when the instance runtime has no MCP methods. base is immutable; a name change or a default_model different from the current one (without template_id) returns 422 beeos_field_not_supported. Not supported by BeeOS Cloud yet (422 beeos_field_not_supported): a non-empty system_prompt, disabled_tools, environment or plugins, or any max_step or timeout_seconds. An unchanged name and empty values are accepted, so a GET-modify-PUT round trip works.

the task reaches a terminal state. With `stream: true` it returns `text/event-stream`

The Agent Plugins manifest schema identifiers this server installs. Present and non-empty
when `capabilities.plugins` is true.

UHPCapabilities.description:
Named booleans. A server reports `false` for a capability it does not implement rather than
omitting it, so a client can distinguish "not supported" from "server predates this field".
A client treats an absent key as `false`.

plugins.description:
The server installs Agent Plugins packages into harnesses, serves their files, and exports
a harness as a package. Optional at every class.

environments.description:
The server holds environments: a project's files and installed dependencies, built once,
read-only at a fixed path in every session that names one. Optional at every class.

memories.description:
The server holds memories: a tree of memories with access granted per node, records kept
by a connected provider, and tools a harness's agent reaches them with. Optional at every class.

base.description:
Opaque. Not enumerated by this specification — a client must treat it as a string, or the
protocol would need revising every time a harness is released.

plugins.description:
Installed plugins. Their servers and skills join the harness's own for every turn;
`mcpServers` and `skills` above report only what was written to them directly.

environment.description:
The environment (`henv_`) this harness's tasks read, mounted read-only at its `mount`;
empty when none. A task may name another with its own `environment` field.

UHPMcpServer.description:
A remote MCP server attached to a harness. Only enabled entries are connected for a turn; a
disabled entry must not be contacted at all. An unreachable server must not fail the task.
Unchanged from 2026-08-11: a process (stdio) server is declared inside a plugin, see
PluginMcpServer.

auth.description:
Bearer token, or a server-side reference the server resolves. A server must never return
a resolved credential to a client.

expires_at.description: BeeOS extension. Expiry of the supplied short-lived credential; the caller refreshes it with another PUT.

UHPPluginMcpServer.description:
An MCP server a plugin's mcp.json declares, derived by the server. The harness MCP server
object plus the `stdio` transport: `url` is required for `http` and `sse`, `command` for
`stdio`. Placeholders are reported unexpanded; `enabled` is always true, the plugin's own
`enabled` governs.

transport.description:
`http` is Streamable HTTP (`streamable-http` in mcp.json); `sse` the older HTTP+SSE
transport; `stdio` a process the server launches inside the agent's sandbox.

headers.description: Fixed request headers (`http` and `sse`). Never subject to placeholder expansion.

command.description:
One executable token (`stdio`): a bare name resolved on the sandbox's search path, or a
plugin-relative path beginning with `./`. Never a shell string, never expanded.

args.description: Arguments (`stdio`). `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` and `${PLUGIN_DATA}` expand at run time.

env.description:
Environment overlay (`stdio`). Must not name PLUGIN_ROOT or PLUGIN_DATA; the server sets
those. Values expand at run time.

cwd.description:
Working directory (`stdio`). Defaults to the plugin root; must stay within the plugin
root or PLUGIN_DATA.

UHPSkill.description:
A skill is a FOLDER, not a file. A server must materialise the whole folder where the agent
can read it — materialising only SKILL.md breaks every skill carrying references, scripts or
data. Round-tripping a harness through GET and PUT must not lose skill contents.

enabled.description: false suppresses the skill, including one inherited from the base.

files.description: The bundle. Must contain a SKILL.md.

content.description: Shorthand for a single-file bundle whose only member is SKILL.md.

blob.description:
Server-assigned handle for a bundle stored out of line. A client receives it, passes it
back unchanged, and reads the files from the skill files endpoint.

sha256.description: BeeOS extension. SHA-256 of the Files bundle referenced by blob.

size_bytes.description: BeeOS extension. Decimal byte size of the Files bundle referenced by blob.

UHPSkillFile.description: One file of a skill folder or of a plugin package.

path.description:
Relative to the skill's own folder, or to the plugin root; nested directories are
supported. A server must reject a path that escapes the folder.

content_b64.description: Base64 for binary content; preserved byte-for-byte.

UHPPlugin.description:
An Agent Plugins package installed into a harness: `plugin.json` at the root, MCP servers in
`mcp.json`, skills under `skills/`. A client writes `files` (or passes back `blob`) and
optionally `name` and `enabled`; the server derives `manifest`, `mcpServers`, `skills` and
`skipped` from the package on every write and ignores those fields on input. A refused
package leaves the harness unchanged.

name.description: The manifest's `name`. Optional on write; if sent it must equal the manifest's.

enabled.description: false keeps the plugin installed and inert; nothing in it is materialised or contacted.

files.description: The package. Must contain `plugin.json` at its root.

blob.description:
Server-assigned handle for a package stored out of line. A client passes it back unchanged
and reads the files from the plugin files endpoint.

mcpServers.description:
Derived from `mcp.json`. Placeholders are reported unexpanded; `enabled` is always true,
the plugin's own `enabled` governs.

skills.description: Derived from `skills/`, one entry per immediate child directory with a SKILL.md.

skipped.description:
What the server found and could not load. Present on every plugin object the server
returns, empty when nothing was skipped.

UHPPluginManifest.description:
`plugin.json`, parsed. Mirrors the Agent Plugins 1.0.0 manifest schema
(https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json, Apache-2.0) field for field, and
permits additional properties because a UHP client ignores fields it does not know. The
schema a manifest's own `$schema` names is authoritative; a server validates against that.

extensions.description: Client-specific data keyed by reverse-domain namespace, per Agent Plugins §8.

name.description: The SKILL.md frontmatter name, equal to the directory name.

default_model.description: BeeOS Cloud honors this only on create; a different value on PUT returns 422 beeos_field_not_supported unless template_id is sent.

mcp_servers.description: Rejected on create (422 beeos_field_not_supported). On PUT the list is diffed against the runtime MCP servers: listed servers are set, omitted ones are unset; 422 beeos_mcp_not_supported only when the instance runtime has no MCP methods.

plugins.description: Requires the `plugins` capability. Each item needs `files` or `blob`.

environment.description: An environment id of the caller's scope, or empty. Requires the `environments` capability.

instance_id.description: BeeOS extension. Instance that hosts a new harness (create only).

template_id.description: BeeOS extension. Agent template applied to the harness.

available.description:
Computed, not asserted: true means the server can serve this model for this harness right
now. Listing a model as available and then failing the task is the worst outcome for a
client, because a user has already chosen it.

input.description: A bare string is shorthand for one user message.

model.description: Model id for this turn. Omitted means the harness default. Any requested id is dispatched as given.

metadata.description:
Client metadata, the extension point of the Responses surface. `harness_id` selects the
configured harness; `environment` names the environment this task reads, overriding the
harness's (capability `environments`), refused with `environment_not_found` or
`environment_not_ready` before the task starts.

stream.description: When true the response is streamed as server-sent events; see `UHPEvent`. Otherwise the call returns the finished response. Defaults to false.

previous_response_id.description: ID of an earlier response to continue. The new response runs in the same session. The earlier response must exist and belong to the same harness.

instructions.description: Instructions placed before the input text and separated from it by a line containing `---`.

store.description: Whether to keep the response so it can be fetched later. Defaults to true.

max_output_tokens.description: Reserved and ignored. It is reported in `metadata.ignored_fields` of the response.

tools.description:
Reserved and ignored. Accepted for wire compatibility, never acted on, and reported in
`metadata.ignored_fields` on the response. A UHP harness invokes and executes tools
itself and reports them in `output`; there is no input path for a tool result, so the
client-executed tool loop this field implies cannot be completed by a conformant server.
Configure tools on the harness instead — see Harnesses §4.1. Tasks §1.4.

include.description:
Reserved and ignored. Accepted for wire compatibility, never acted on, and reported in
`metadata.ignored_fields` on the response. No values are enumerated, so any string a
server recognised would be one it named itself. Tasks §1.4.

background.description: When true on a request that is not streamed, the call returns at once with the response still `in_progress`; fetch the result later. Ignored when `stream` is true.

id.description: ID of the response. It starts with `resp_`.

status.description: Status of the response. See `UHPResponseStatus` for the values.

incomplete_details.description: Why the response is incomplete. When `status` is `incomplete` it holds `reason`: `max_tokens` or `timeout`. Otherwise null.

previous_response_id.description: ID of the response this one continues, when the request set `previous_response_id`.

output.description: Output items produced so far, in order.

store.description: Whether the response is kept so it can be fetched later.

usage.description:
null when the server cannot account for usage. A fabricated zero would be worse than an
honest absence, because a client cannot tell it from a free task.

session_id.description: ID of the session the response ran in. Responses chained with `previous_response_id` share it.

environment.description: The environment the task read, when it read one (capability `environments`).

requested_model.description: The id the client sent, when the client sent one.

model_fallback.description: True only when the harness reported it could not switch to the requested model.

ignored_fields.description:
Request fields the server did not act on, by name, in any order. Required when the
request carried `tools` or `include`, which are reserved and ignored. A silently
ignored field is indistinguishable from an honoured one. Tasks §1.1 and §1.4.

UHPResponseStatus.description:
`incomplete` means a budget stopped the work and is usually worth continuing.
`failed` means it could not be done. `cancelled` means the client asked for a stop, and must
never be reported as `failed`.

x-enumDescriptions.failed: The work could not be done.
x-enumDescriptions.incomplete: A limit, such as the output limit or the time limit, stopped the work. It is usually worth continuing.
x-enumDescriptions.cancelled: The client asked to stop. A cancelled response is never reported as `failed`.

UHPOutputItem.description:
A client must tolerate item types it does not recognise. A client that renders only `message`
items and ignores the rest is a valid client.

type.description: Kind of the output item. Clients should ignore item types they do not know.

x-enumDescriptions.message: A message written by the agent. Its text is in `content`.
x-enumDescriptions.reasoning: The agent's reasoning. Its summary is in `summary`.
x-enumDescriptions.function_call: A tool call made by the agent, with `name` and `arguments`.
x-enumDescriptions.function_call_output: The result of a tool call, in `output`.

x-enumDescriptions.in_progress: The item is still being produced.

call_id.description: ID of the function call. A `function_call_output` item refers to its call with the same `call_id`.

name.description: Name of the function the agent called.

output.description: Result of the function call, as text.

x-enumDescriptions.output_text: Text of a `message` item, with optional annotations.

annotations.description: Annotations that refer to ranges of `text`.

x-enumDescriptions.container_file_citation: The text refers to a file produced by the agent.

container_id.description: ID of the container that holds the file. BeeOS does not currently set it.

file_id.description: ID of the file. BeeOS does not currently set it.

download_url.description: Absolute URL the file can be downloaded from.

start_index.description: Start of the cited range in the text, counted in characters. BeeOS sets it to 0.

end_index.description: End of the cited range in the text, counted in characters. BeeOS sets it to the length of the text.

cache_read_tokens.description: Input tokens read from the cache.

cache_write_tokens.description: Input tokens written to the cache.

detail.description:
A human-readable alias of `error.message`, retained for clients written against
implementations that predate this envelope. Carries no information not in `error`.

type.description: Category of the error. It follows from the HTTP status.

x-enumDescriptions.invalid_request_error: The request is invalid or refers to something that does not exist or conflicts with current state.
x-enumDescriptions.authentication_error: The API key is missing or invalid.
x-enumDescriptions.permission_error: The API key does not have the scope the call needs.
x-enumDescriptions.harness_error: The harness failed to do what was asked.
x-enumDescriptions.server_error: The server could not serve the request.

code.description:
Specific and machine-readable. Servers may define additional codes for conditions this
specification does not cover, and must namespace them with a vendor prefix so a future
version cannot collide with them.

message.description:
One sentence, safe to show a user. Must not contain credentials, internal hostnames, file
paths, or stack traces.

param.description: Dotted path to the offending field.

detail.description: Additional structured detail about the error, when available.

UHPEvent.description:
One streamed event. `sequence_number` starts at 0 and increases by exactly 1 per event, so a
client can detect a dropped event rather than silently rendering a gap.

type.description: Kind of the event. Clients should ignore event types they do not know. Exactly one of `response.completed`, `response.incomplete` and `response.failed` ends a stream.

x-enumDescriptions.response.created: The response was created. `response` is the initial snapshot with status `in_progress`.
x-enumDescriptions.response.in_progress: The response is running. `response` is a snapshot.
x-enumDescriptions.response.output_item.added: A new output item started. `item` is its initial form and `output_index` its position in the output.
x-enumDescriptions.response.output_item.done: An output item is complete. `item` is its final form.
x-enumDescriptions.response.content_part.added: A content part was added to a `message` item. `part` is its initial form.
x-enumDescriptions.response.content_part.done: A content part of a `message` item is complete. `part` is its final form.
x-enumDescriptions.response.output_text.delta: More text was appended to the text of a `message` item. `delta` is the new text.
x-enumDescriptions.response.output_text.done: The text of a `message` item is complete. `text` is the full text.
x-enumDescriptions.response.output_text.annotation.added: An annotation, such as a file citation, was added to the text of a `message` item.
x-enumDescriptions.response.reasoning_summary_part.added: A summary part was added to a `reasoning` item.
x-enumDescriptions.response.reasoning_summary_text.delta: More text was appended to the summary of a `reasoning` item. `delta` is the new text.
x-enumDescriptions.response.reasoning_summary_part.done: A summary part of a `reasoning` item is complete. `part` is its final form.
x-enumDescriptions.response.function_call_arguments.delta: The arguments of a `function_call` item were written. `delta` holds the arguments text.
x-enumDescriptions.response.function_call_arguments.done: The arguments of a `function_call` item are complete. `arguments` holds them as a JSON string.
x-enumDescriptions.response.completed: The response finished successfully. This is a terminal event: exactly one terminal event ends the stream.
x-enumDescriptions.response.incomplete: The response stopped because of a limit, for example the output limit or the time limit. This is a terminal event.
x-enumDescriptions.response.failed: The response failed or was cancelled; `response.status` is `failed` or `cancelled`. This is a terminal event.
x-enumDescriptions.error: An error that did not end the response. `code`, `message` and `param` describe it, and a terminal event still follows.
x-enumDescriptions.beeos.approval.requested: BeeOS extension. The agent asks for approval of an action. The `approval` property holds the approval request document.
x-enumDescriptions.beeos.approval.resolved: BeeOS extension. An approval request was resolved. The `approval` property holds the resolution document.

sequence_number.description: Position of the event in the stream, starting at 0 and increasing by 1 per event. A gap means an event was lost.

response.description: Snapshot of the response. Present on lifecycle events.

item.description: The output item. Present on `response.output_item.added` and `response.output_item.done`.

part.description: The content or summary part. Present on content part and reasoning summary part events.

delta.description: New text, or new function arguments, since the previous delta.

arguments.description: The complete function arguments as a JSON string. Present on `response.function_call_arguments.done`.

item_id.description: ID of the output item the event belongs to.

output_index.description: Position of the item in the `output` of the response.

content_index.description: Index of the content part within the item.

summary_index.description: Index of the summary part within the item.

annotation_index.description: Index of the annotation within the content part.

code.description: Machine-readable error code. Present on `error` events.

message.description: Readable error message. Present on `error` events.

param.description: Dotted path of the field the error is about, or null. Present on `error` events.

JSONValue.description: A genuinely open JSON value (provider/plugin parameters or arbitrary metadata).

organization_id.description: ID of the organization that owns the instance.

app_id.description: ID of the app the instance belongs to.

developer_id.description: ID of the developer account the instance was created under.

harness.description: Product harness name (for example `openclaw`), not a UHP `harness_id` (`chrn_*`).

provider_id.description: ID of the provider that hosts the instance.

region.description: Region the instance is deployed in.

os_type.description: Operating system of the instance: `linux`, `windows`, `android` or `macos`.

status.description: Lifecycle phase of the instance: `pending`, `provisioning`, `running`, `stopped` or `terminated`.

desired_status.description: Lifecycle phase the instance is being driven toward: `running`, `stopped` or `terminated`.

connectivity.description: Reachability of the instance's agent: `unknown`, `online` or `offline`.

error_code.description: Stable code describing a failure or degraded state reported with a lifecycle result, for example `quota_exceeded`, `capacity_pending`, `provision_failed` or `stop_failed`. Raw provider errors are never exported.

ms_connection_status.description: Status of the instance's message-channel connection: `unknown`, `connecting`, `connected`, `reconnecting`, `disconnected` or `failed`. It is reported independently of connectivity and is `unknown` while the instance is stopped or terminated, or has not reported recently.

image_id.description: ID of the platform image the instance runs.

image_version_id.description: ID of the platform image version the instance runs.

image_version.description: Version label of the platform image the instance runs.

image_ref.description: Pinned public image reference. Provider configuration is never included.

model_primary.description: Primary model configured for the instance.

llm.description: Model providers and models supplied for the instance, with API keys removed.

hosting_type.description: Where the instance is hosted: `cloud` or `selfhosted`.

image_slot.description: Variant trait. Key that selects the execution image for the instance. Not a container repository name.

worker_image_id.description: Variant trait. AgentBay worker image. Never the platform `image_id`.

model_catalog.description: Variant trait. `served` when Cloud answers model-list and reasoning-level requests, `none` when it answers neither. Empty and unknown values behave as `none`.

billing_slot.description: Variant trait. Key into the monthly fee table that prices the instance.

icon_key.description: Variant trait. UI icon selector. Clients must not derive it from `harness`.

device_control.description: Variant trait. Whether the instance accepts device-control commands. False means those commands are rejected.

runtime_profile.description: Variant trait. Profile of the agent runtime the instance uses. Known values are `openclaw`, `hermes` and `beeos-browser`.

free_plan.description: Variant trait. Whether the free plan allows the instance's variant. False means the free plan does not allow it.

resource_version.description: Version of the instance record, starting at 1. Send it in the `If-Match` header of write requests so concurrent changes are detected.

has_ever_run.description: Whether the instance has ever reached the running state. False means it has never delivered a running service.

created_at.description: Time the instance was created, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp.

updated_at.description: Time the instance was last updated, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp.

capabilities.description: Capabilities declared for the instance when it was provisioned, as flags such as `computer`, `mobile`, `device` and `terminal`. An empty object means none were declared.

phase.description: Phase of the operation: `intent`, `reserved`, `admitted`, `provisioning`, `running`, `cleanup_pending`, `failed`, `stop_pending`, `stopped`, `delete_pending`, `deleted`, `upgrade_pending` or `rollback_pending`. It describes durable work, not observed instance health.

error_code.description: Stable failure code, the same value as the instance `error_code`. Raw provider errors are never exported.

data.description: The instance as of this response.

operation.description: Lifecycle operation that this response reports on.

stdout.description: Standard output of the command, at most 64 KiB.

stderr.description: Standard error of the command, at most 64 KiB.

providers.description: Model provider endpoints, 1 to 8 entries. Every provider must be referenced by at least one model.

models.description: Selectable models, 1 to 256 entries. Exactly one has the `default` role.

providers.description: Model provider endpoints, without API keys.

id.description: Caller-chosen ID that models refer to. It is unique within the request, 1 to 64 characters from `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-`.

protocol.description: API protocol the endpoint speaks: `openai` or `anthropic`.

base_url.description: HTTPS base URL of the provider API, at most 512 characters. It must not contain credentials, a query string or a fragment.

api_key.description: API key for the provider, 1 to 4096 characters without whitespace. It is write-only and never returned.

id.description: ID of the provider, as referenced by models.

protocol.description: API protocol the endpoint speaks: `openai` or `anthropic`.

base_url.description: HTTPS base URL of the provider API.

provider_id.description: ID of the provider that serves the model.

model.description: Model name as the provider API expects it. It is unique per provider.

role.description: Role of the model: `default`, `fallback` or `available`. Exactly one model is `default`. Automatic failover uses only `fallback` models.

order.description: Position of the model, unique across all models. The `default` model has order 0; `fallback` and `available` models have order 1 or more.

job_id.description: Unique ID of the upgrade job.

instance_id.description: ID of the instance being upgraded.

target.description: Image version the instance is being upgraded to.

created_at.description: Time the job was created, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp.

completed_at.description: Time the job finished, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp. Omitted while the job is not finished.

error.description: Stable failure code. Omitted unless the job failed.

name.description: Display name of the instance, 1 to 128 bytes, without leading or trailing whitespace.

variant_id.description: ID of the catalog variant to create the instance from, at most 128 characters. See the instance template catalog for available variants. An unknown ID returns 404 `variant_not_found`.

harness.description: Harness to run in the instance. Only `openclaw` is accepted.

llm.description: Model providers and models the instance uses. Required when the variant or harness needs caller-supplied models; omit it for variants that supply their own models. Provider API keys are write-only.

status.description: Lifecycle phase of the instance: `pending`, `provisioning`, `running`, `stopped` or `terminated`.

desired_status.description: Lifecycle phase the instance is being driven toward: `running`, `stopped` or `terminated`.

connectivity.description: Reachability of the instance's agent: `unknown`, `online` or `offline`.

operation.description: Lifecycle operation that this response reports on.

name.description: New display name, 1 to 128 characters, without leading or trailing whitespace. Send `name`, `llm` or both.

llm.description: Replacement model providers and models. It replaces the whole existing llm block. Provider API keys are write-only. When `name` is also sent, the llm block is replaced first.

slug.description: Public slug that identifies the share.

framework.description: Agent framework of the instance the agent runs on.

agent.description: The agent that wrote the reply.

parts.description: Content of the reply. It holds one part of type `text`.

created_at.description: Time the reply message was created.

title.description: Title of the source, when the agent provided one.

sources.description: Web sources the reply cites. Only `https` sources are listed.

files.description: Files the reply links to. Only files published by BeeOS are listed.

url.description: URL to connect to. For `browser` it is the browser viewer URL; for `acp` it is a WebSocket URL that already carries the access ticket as a query parameter.

token.description: Short-lived access token for the browser viewer. Not returned for `acp`.

service.description: Service the URL connects to: `browser` or `acp`.

stream_session_id.description: ID of the viewing client session, the `client_id` sent in the request. Not returned for `acp`.

grant_id.description: ID of the browser access grant.

generation.description: Generation of the browser the grant is bound to. When `generation` was sent in the request, it equals that value.

role.description: Access role of the grant: `viewer` or `controller`.

browser.description: Browser access grant. Returned only for `browser`.

data.description: Connection details for the requested service.

kid.description: ID of the key that signed the ticket.

aud.description: Audience the ticket is intended for: the terminal service.

sub.description: ID of the external user the ticket was issued for, from the `X-BeeOS-External-User-ID` header.

instance_id.description: ID of the instance the terminal belongs to.

platform_agent_id.description: ID of the agent the terminal session is for, the `platformAgentId` of the request.

client_id.description: ID generated for this terminal client connection.

conversation_id.description: ID of the conversation the terminal is attached to. Present only when the request sent `conversationId`.

resume_terminal_id.description: ID of the terminal to resume. Present only when the request sent `resumeTerminalId`.

iat.description: Time the ticket was issued, in Unix seconds.

exp.description: Time the ticket expires, in Unix seconds.

sub.description: ID of the external user the ticket was issued for, from the `X-BeeOS-External-User-ID` header.

instance_id.description: ID of the instance the canvas belongs to.

platform_agent_id.description: ID of the agent the canvas session is for, the `platformAgentId` of the request.

client_id.description: ID generated for this relay client connection.

conversation_id.description: ID of the conversation the canvas belongs to, the `conversationId` of the request.

canvas_id.description: ID of the canvas the ticket grants access to.

role.description: Access role granted on the canvas: `viewer` or `editor`.

session_id.description: ID of the realtime session created for this ticket.

aud.description: Audiences the ticket is intended for: the canvas relay.

iat.description: Time the ticket was issued, in Unix seconds.

exp.description: Time the ticket expires, in Unix seconds.

protocolVersion.description: Version of the ticket protocol. Currently 1.

websocketUrl.description: WebSocket URL to open the terminal connection on. It already carries the ticket as a query parameter.

ticket.description: Signed single-use ticket (a JWT) that authorizes one terminal connection. It is valid for 60 seconds.

issuedAt.description: Time the ticket was issued, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

expiresAt.description: Time the ticket expires, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Tickets are valid for 60 seconds.

claims.description: Claims contained in the signed ticket.

protocolVersion.description: Version of the ticket protocol. Currently 1.

relayUrl.description: WebSocket URL of the canvas relay for the canvas, ending in `/ws/{canvasId}`.

ticket.description: Signed single-use ticket (a JWT) that authorizes one relay connection. It is valid for 60 seconds.

issuedAt.description: Time the ticket was issued, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

expiresAt.description: Time the ticket expires, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Tickets are valid for 60 seconds.

claims.description: Claims contained in the signed ticket.

NotFound.description:
No such object in the caller's scope. Servers return 404 rather than 403 for objects outside
the caller's scope, so that an id's existence is not disclosed.

UHPVersion.description: The protocol version actually used to serve this response.

MessageContentChatMessage.description: Content of a prompt sent to the agent.

MessageContentAgentReply.description: Content of an agent reply. A successful reply carries `text`; a failed one carries `error`.

error.description: Error message when the reply is a failure.

MessageContentAgentRefuse.description: Content of a message in which the agent declines the task.

reason.description: Why the agent declined, for example `agent_busy`.

MessageContentChatCancel.description: Content of a request to stop the agent's turn.

target_message_id.description: ID of the `chat_message` whose turn should stop.

reason.description: Why the turn should stop: `canceled`, `caller_disconnected` or `timeout`.

MessageContentDeviceCommand.description: Content of a device tool call.

tool.description: Name of the device tool to run, for example `screenshot`, `click` or `tap`.

args.description: Arguments of the tool; they depend on the tool.

channel_id.description: ID of the conversation the command belongs to.

context_id.description: ID of the conversation the command belongs to.

MessageContentDeviceError.description: Content of the failure of a device tool call.

code.description: Kind of failure reported by the device tool, for example `unsupported`, `invalid_args` or `internal_error`.

MessagePartText.description: A piece of the reply text.

MessagePartThinking.description: A piece of the agent's reasoning.

state.description: Whether the reasoning is still being written.

x-enumDescriptions.streaming: The part is still being written.
x-enumDescriptions.done: The part is complete. A missing state also means done.

MessagePartToolUse.description: A tool call made by the agent.

id.description: ID of the tool call. A `tool_result` part refers to it with `tool_use_id`.

arguments.description: Arguments of the call as JSON.

state.description: Whether the arguments are still being written.

x-enumDescriptions.streaming: The part is still being written.
x-enumDescriptions.done: The part is complete. A missing state also means done.

MessagePartToolResult.description: The result of a tool call.

tool_use_id.description: ID of the `tool_use` part this result belongs to.

content.description: Result of the tool: a JSON object or a plain string.

MessagePartFile.description: A file attached to the message. Images, audio and video are all `file` parts; tell them apart by `mime_type`.

mime_type.description: MIME type of the file, for example `image/png`.

size.description: Size of the file in bytes.

MessagePartCustom.description: An extension part for structured content that has no dedicated type. `kind` says what the part is.

kind.description: What kind of custom part this is.

data.description: Payload of the part as JSON; it depends on `kind`.

UHPEventResponse.description: A response lifecycle event that carries a snapshot of the response.

part.description: The content or summary part. Present on content part and reasoning summary part events.
